topic.name: The Sum of the First N Terms of a Geometric Series

question.text: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $3+15+75+\cdots\,?$
question.explanation:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

\begin{align} r &= \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{15}{3}\\[5pt] &= 5 \end{align}

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

\[ S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}. \]

In this case $a_1=3$ and $r=5.$ Substituting these values into the formula for $S_N$ gives the following:

\begin{align} S_N &= \dfrac{a_1(1-r^N)}{1-r}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3\left(1-5^N\right)}{1-5}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3\left(1-5^N\right)}{(-4)}\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{3}{4}\left(1-5^N\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{4}\left(5^N-1\right) \end{align}

question.text: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $2+6+18+\cdots?$
question.explanation:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

\begin{align} r &= \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{6}{2}\\[5pt] &= 3 \end{align}

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

\[ S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}. \]

In this case, $a_1= 2$ and $r = 3.$ Therefore, we have:

\begin{align} S_N &= \dfrac{2(1-3^N)}{1 - 3}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{2}(1-3^N)\\[5pt] &= 3^N-1 \end{align}

question.text: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series $6+18+54+\cdots?$
question.explanation:
First, we determine the common ratio $r$ for this geometric series:

\begin{align} r &= \dfrac{a_2}{a_1} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{18}{6}\\[5pt] &= 3 \end{align}

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

\[ S_N = \dfrac{a_1 \left(1-r^N\right) }{1-r}. \]

In this case, $a_1= 6$ and $r = 3.$ Substituting these values into the formula for $S_N$ gives the following:

\begin{align} S_N &= \dfrac{6\left(1-3^N\right)}{1 - 3} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{6}{2}\left(1-3^N\right) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3\left( 3^N-1 \right)} \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given the First Few Terms

question.text: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $7$th term is $512$ and the common ratio is $2?$ Express your answer as a function of $N,$ making sure you use a capital letter $(N,$ not $n).$
question.explanation:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine $a_1\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} a_n &= a_1r^{n-1} \\[5pt] % a_7 &= a_1 \cdot 2^{7-1} \\[5pt] 512 &= a_1\cdot 2^{(7-1)} \\[5pt] 512 &= 64a_1 \\[5pt] a_1 &= 8 \end{align}

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula \[ S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r} . \]

In this case, $a_1=8$ and $r=2.$ Substituting our values into the formula for $S_N$ gives \begin{align} S_N &= \dfrac{8(1-2^N)}{1-2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8(1-2^N)}{(-1)} \\[5pt] &= -8(1-2^N) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{8(2^N-1)}. \end{align}
